title.full: What IP riders cover and cost

summary.text: IP riders can reduce some out-of-pocket costs, but premiums are paid in cash and rise with age. Consider affordability and value.

details.heading: What an IP rider does
details.body: An IP rider is optional. It covers part of your Integrated Shield Plan deductible and co-insurance. You must still co-pay at least 5% of the claimable amount.

details.heading: Other possible coverage
details.body: Some riders may cover extra treatments, including cancer drug treatments not covered under MediShield Life and IPs. IPs and riders may also cover pre- and post-hospitalisation, emergency overseas treatments and Traditional Chinese Medicine.

details.heading: What to consider
details.body: Consider whether lower co-pay is worth the extra premiums. Also consider whether extra coverage is worth the cost. Most importantly, make sure you can afford the rider over the long term, as premiums increase with age.

details.heading: How premiums are paid
details.body: Rider premiums can only be paid in cash.

sources.page_title: What are IP riders and should I consider getting one?

quotes.text: IP riders are optional products designed to cover part of the deductible and co-insurance of your Integrated Shield Plan (IP).
Even with a rider, patients will still need to co-pay a minimum of 5% of the claimable amount.
Riders may also provide coverage for additional treatments, such as cancer drug treatments not covered under MediShield Life and IPs.

Most importantly, consider whether you can afford a rider in the long run. As you age, your premiums will increase and may strain your finances if not planned for adequately, leading to affordability issues in later years.
Riders premiums can only be paid in cash.
